title: Marvelous College Entrance Exam
synopsis: It is no exaggeration to say that the college entrance exam in China can decide your entire future. Here we learn to what lengths some parents will go to help their children study for it.

fullText.simplified:
那些高考的奇葩事儿

    高考，是普通高等学校招生全国统一考试的简称，是中国大学最重要的入学考试。在中国，大学没有自己的入学考试，能否进入好的大学，都是靠高考的分数来决定的，而高考每年只有一次。每个人都想进入好的大学，因为如果能进入好的大学，那就意味着将来能找到好的工作，认识许多优秀的人，以后的人生道路会越来越好。所以在中国，人们常说“一考定终身”，从这句话，就可以看出中国人对于高考有多么重视了。特别是现在中国都是独生子女家庭，家长把所有的希望都寄托在孩子的身上，所以决定孩子未来的高考，已经不是孩子个人的事情了，而是整个家庭，甚至是学校、社会都摆在第一位的事情。
    下面就来看看一些家长们，为了孩子的高考疯狂到什么地步吧。
    有的家长在高考期间，为了给孩子创造一个绝对安静的环境，主动联合起来走上街头，见人拦人，见车拦车，甚至与不配合的司机发生了冲突。
    这还算好的。有的家长，为了孩子能专心学习，恨不得全世界都围着他孩子转。重庆某个小区的一户人家，认为家门口的电梯运行的时候有噪音，影响了自己孩子的休息，于是要求小区停止运行电梯。结果96户居民，只能每天爬楼梯。更有甚者，认为小区周围的青蛙叫，影响了孩子的学习，于是下毒，把青蛙全都给毒死了。
    除了在给孩子创造一个安静的环境上下功夫外，家长们还喜欢去拜寺庙，祈求孩子能考出好的成绩。拜寺庙，是一种信仰，本来是挺好的一件事，但是有的家长，非常疯狂，专门跑到外地去拜卧佛寺，只因为卧佛寺读起来像英文的“office”，他们说拜了卧佛寺，孩子将来毕业了就能进国外的企业，给外国人打工，工资高。还有的家长，对送孩子去考场时用的车非常讲究。车牌号码不能是零、四、六，因为“零’代表“零分”，“四”读起来像“死”，“六”和“落”同音，意味着高考落榜。更有的家长，希望开车的师傅最好是姓马的，因为中国有句成语，叫“马到成功”。
    这些在我们看起来非常好笑，不符合常理的事情，家长们为了孩子，都是很认真地在做。有很多事情，其实他们也知道不一定有用，但是他们还是在做。因为只要是为了孩子的，只要是有一点作用的，他们都会拼命地去做。“可怜天下父母心”，现在社会的竞争压力太大，决定孩子命运的高考不仅让孩子，也让家长们过于紧张，这些也许也是家长们舒缓心理压力的一种方法吧。
fullText.traditional:
那些高考的奇葩事兒

    高考，是普通高等學校招生全國統一考試的簡稱，是中國大學最重要的入學考試。在中國，大學沒有自己的入學考試，能否進入好的大學，都是靠高考的分數來決定的，而高考每年只有一次。每個人都想進入好的大學，因為如果能進入好的大學，那就意味著將來能找到好的工作，認識許多優秀的人，以後的人生道路會越來越好。所以在中國，人們常說“一考定終身”，從這句話，就可以看出中國人對於高考有多麼重視了。特別是現在中國都是獨生子女家庭，家長把所有的希望都寄託在孩子的身上，所以決定孩子未來的高考，已經不是孩子個人的事情了，而是整個家庭，甚至是學校、社會都擺在第一位的事情。
    下面就來看看一些家長們，為了孩子的高考瘋狂到什麼地步吧。
    有的家長在高考期間，為了給孩子創造一個絕對安靜的環境，主動聯合起來走上街頭，見人攔人，見車攔車，甚至與不配合的司機發生了衝突。
    這還算好的。有的家長，為了孩子能專心學習，恨不得全世界都圍著他孩子轉。重慶某個小區的一戶人家，認為家門口的電梯運行的時候有噪音，影響了自己孩子的休息，於是要求小區停止運行電梯。結果96戶居民，只能每天爬樓梯。更有甚者，認為小區周圍的青蛙叫，影響了孩子的學習，於是下毒，把青蛙全都給毒死了。
    除了在給孩子創造一個安靜的環境上下功夫外，家長們還喜歡去拜寺廟，祈求孩子能考出好的成績。拜寺廟，是一種信仰，本來是挺好的一件事，但是有的家長，非常瘋狂，專門跑到外地去拜臥佛寺，只因為臥佛寺讀起來像英文的“office”，他們說拜了臥佛寺，孩子將來畢業了就能進國外的企業，給外國人打工，工資高。還有的家長，對送孩子去考場時用的車非常講究。車牌號碼不能是零、四、六，因為“零’代表“零分”，“四”讀起來像“死”，“六”和“落”同音，意味著高考落榜。更有的家長，希望開車的師傅最好是姓馬的，因為中國有句成語，叫“馬到成功”。
    這些在我們看起來非常好笑，不符合常理的事情，家長們為了孩子，都是很認真地在做。有很多事情，其實他們也知道不一定有用，但是他們還是在做。因為只要是為了孩子的，只要是有一點作用的，他們都會拼命地去做。“可憐天下父母心”，現在社會的競爭壓力太大，決定孩子命運的高考不僅讓孩子，也讓家長們過於緊張，這些也許也是家長們舒緩心理壓力的一種方法吧。

sentences.traditional: 這些在我們看起來非常好笑，不符合常理的事情，家長們為了孩子，都是很認真地在做。
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiē zài wǒ men kàn qǐ lái fēi cháng hǎo xiào bù fú hé cháng lǐ de shì qing jiā zhǎng men wèi le hái zi dōu shì hěn rèn zhēn de zài zuò

sentences.simplified: 有很多事情，其实他们也知道不一定有用，但是他们还是在做。
sentences.traditional: 有很多事情，其實他們也知道不一定有用，但是他們還是在做。
sentences.pinyin: yǒu hěn duō shì qing qí shí tā men yě zhī dào bù yí dìng yǒu yòng dàn shì tā men hái shì zài zuò
sentences.english: To us this might seem laughable and lacking common sense, but these family heads will eagerly do anything for their children.

sentences.simplified: 因为只要是为了孩子的，只要是有一点作用的，他们都会拼命地去做。
sentences.traditional: 因為只要是為了孩子的，只要是有一點作用的，他們都會拼命地去做。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi zhǐ yào shì wèi le hái zi de zhǐ yào shì yǒu yì diǎn zuò yòng de tā men dōu huì pīn mìng de qù zuò
sentences.english: Many of these things the family heads are actually aware that they might not actually have any use, but they will still do it.

sentences.simplified: “可怜天下父母心”，
sentences.traditional: “可憐天下父母心”，
sentences.pinyin: kě lián tiān xià fù mǔ xīn
sentences.english: Because as long as it is for their child, and it might have just a little bit of effect, they will do it to their heart's consent.

sentences.simplified: 现在社会的竞争压力太大，
sentences.traditional: 現在社會的競爭壓力太大，
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài shè huì de jìng zhēng yā lì tài dà
sentences.english: “The poor parents of the world constantly worry about their children”

sentences.simplified: 决定孩子命运的高考不仅让孩子，也让家长们过于紧张，
sentences.traditional: 決定孩子命運的高考不僅讓孩子，也讓家長們過於緊張，
sentences.pinyin: jué dìng hái zi mìng yùn de gāo kǎo bù jǐn ràng hái zi yě ràng jiā zhǎng men guò yú jǐn zhāng
sentences.english: The competitive pressure in today's society is too high.

sentences.simplified: 这些也许也是家长们舒缓心理压力的一种方法吧。
sentences.traditional: 這些也許也是家長們舒緩心理壓力的一種方法吧。
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiē yě xǔ yě shì jiā zhǎng men shū huǎn xīn lǐ yā lì de yì zhǒng fāng fǎ ba
sentences.english: The “gao kao” which decides a child's future does not only make the child, but also the parents overly nervous.

raw.synopsis: It is no exaggeration to say that the college entrance exam in China can decide your entire future. Here we learn to what lengths some parents will go to help their children study for it.
sentence_translations: Those Marvelous Things Before the College Entrance Exam
“Gao kao” is the short name for the common university enrollment national exam.
It is the most important exam for entering a university in China.
In China, universities do not have their own entrance exams.
Whether or not you can enter a good university is all decided by the “gao kao”, and there is only one exam per year.
Everyone wants to enter a good university, because entering a good university means you can find a good job in the future, ..
.. that you can get to know talented people, and will have an easier path in life.
So in China, people often say “one exam that decides your life”.
From these words you can make out just how much the Chinese value the “gao kao”.
Especially now when a lot of Chinese families have only one child, the family head places all their hopes on this child.
So the “gao kao” which decides the child's future, is no longer just about the child itself, but the entire family.
Even the schools and the whole society make the “gao pao” a top priority.
Following, we will take a look at some crazy things some family heads will do for their child's entrance exam.
To give their children a peaceful studying environment, some family heads get together in the streets during the exam period.
If they see a person, they block them. If they see a car, they block it. They will even get into fights with drivers who won't comply.
But this is nothing.
Some family heads wish to make the entire world revolve around their child, to let them focus on their studies.
In a housing estate in Chongqing, a family thought the elevator outside the apartment made noise when it moved, ..
.. which influenced their resting child. They thus demanded that the housing estate shut down the elevator.
As a result, 96 resident families had no choice but to take the stairs every day.
Furthermore, they believed the frogs making noise around the housing estate influenced their child's studies.
And because of this, they killed all the frogs with poison.
Apart from putting effort into giving the child a peaceful environment, ..
.. the family heads also like to visit temples to pray that their children will get good marks on the exam.
Visiting temples is a type of faith, and is originally something good.
But some family heads go crazy and go all the way to visit the Wat Pho temple, ..
.. only because the Chinese pronunciation of Wat Pho sounds like “office” in English.
They say that by visiting Wat Pho, the child will enter a foreign company in the future.
Working for foreigners, their salary will be high.
There are also some family heads who are very particular about the car they use to take their child to the exam.
The car number must not contain zero, four or six, ..
.. because zero symbolizes 0 points, four is pronounced like “death”, and six sounds like “fail” as in failing the exam.
Some family heads also want the driver's name to be Ma, because there is a Chinese proverb “to achieve instant success”.
To us this might seem laughable and lacking common sense, but these family heads will eagerly do anything for their children.
Many of these things the family heads are actually aware that they might not actually have any use, but they will still do it.
Because as long as it is for their child, and it might have just a little bit of effect, they will do it to their heart's consent.
“The poor parents of the world constantly worry about their children”
The competitive pressure in today's society is too high.
The “gao kao” which decides a child's future does not only make the child, but also the parents overly nervous.
These methods are perhaps just a way for these family heads to ease some of this mental pressure.
